title: Optimized protocol for tRNA identification in the ribosomal complexes from human cell lines
protocol: Transfect V5-TEV-NEMF and control vector (V5-TEV-NEMF D96A or V5-NEMF) into cells prepared above.
Add 150 μg of pcDNA-V5-TEV-NEMF wild type, the D96A mutant, or the V5-NEMF wild type without a TEV protease recognition motif to a 50 mL tube for each 500 cm² plate.
Add 50 μg of p5FBG-Nonstop per tube.
Mix gently by pipetting after adding Opti-MEM to a final volume of 7 mL.
Prepare PEI-Max solution in a separate 50 mL tube by adding 600 μL of PEI-Max transfection reagent and mixing with 7 mL of Opti-MEM.
Stand the prepared solutions at 20°C–24°C for 5 min.
Incubate PEI-Max solution for 5 minutes.
Mix plasmid solution with PEI-Max solution by pipetting.
Stand the mixture at 20°C–24°C for 20 minutes.
Add the transfection complex to cell cultures on 500 cm² plates.
Replace the medium with 75 mL of DMEM containing 10% FBS 4 hours after adding the transfection complex.
Incubate for 24 hours.
Prepare plasmids using a transfection-grade purification kit and store at -20°C at a concentration of 1 mg/mL.
Transfer 300 μL of Protein G Dynabeads into a 1.5 mL tube.
Place the tube on a magnetic rack, let it stand for one minute, and discard supernatant by pipetting.
Remove tube from magnetic rack and add 600 μL of Lysis buffer and 60 μL of anti-V5 antibody.
Rotate at 10 rpm at 4°C for 1 hour.
Place the tube on a magnetic rack, let it stand for one minute, and discard supernatant by pipetting.
Remove tube from magnetic rack and wash beads with 600 μL of Lysis buffer twice.
Add 250 μL of Lysis buffer and keep on ice.
Prepare one 10%–35% linear sucrose gradient per sample in open-top polyclear tubes.
Mark a line on the side of the open-top polyclear tubes for SW28 using Marker Block.
Pour 10% sucrose until the marked line.
Layer 35% sucrose from the bottom of the tube using a syringe.
Cap the tubes with Long caps for SW28 tubes.
Place the tubes on a tube holder.
Run a program for 10%–35% linear sucrose gradient on Gradient Master.
Place the gradients on a tube holder at 4°C until use.
Decant the medium from the plate.
Pour 30 mL of prewarmed D-PBS supplemented with 100 μg/mL cycloheximide onto each plate.
Place the plate back into a 5% CO2 incubator for 10 minutes.
Decant the D-PBS from the plates.
Place the plates on ice and add 15 mL of ice-cold D-PBS supplemented with 100 μg/mL cycloheximide per plate.
Scrape the cells and transfer them into a 50 mL tube, collecting cells from the same genotype in the same tube.
Spin down the cells at 5000 g for 1 minute.
Aspirate the PBS carefully from the cell pellets.
Resuspend each cell pellet with 1 mL of lysis buffer per sample supplemented with protease inhibitors, RNasin RNase inhibitor, and cycloheximide.
Transfer the lysates into a 2 mL microcentrifuge tube per sample.
Keep the tubes on ice for 10 minutes.
Centrifuge the samples at 20000 g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Collect the supernatant in a new 2 mL tube.
Repeat centrifugation and collect the supernatant in a new 1.5 mL tube.
Keep 20 μL of each lysate as input.
Add 280 μL of ddH2O to the remaining lysate.
Add 300 μL of acidic phenol (pH 4.2) to the mixture and vortex vigorously.
Keep the mixture on ice until RNA extraction is performed.
Decant the medium from the plate.
Pour D-PBS directly into the plate without using an aspirator or pipettor.
Keep the scraper on ice before use for cell collection.
Scrape cells using a large plastic dough scraper to collect them efficiently.
Layer the lysate from two 500 cm² plates per sample onto a 10%–35% sucrose gradient.
Centrifuge at 27000 g for 2.5 hours at 4°C with an SW28 rotor, using maximum acceleration and deceleration.
After centrifugation, fractionate the sucrose gradients using a Piston Gradient Fractionator.
Pool the 60S ribosome fractions into a 15 mL tube per sample (approximately 3 mL per sample).
Keep aside input samples before loading all lysate to the gradient.
Balance the sample tubes before proceeding with centrifugation.
Adjust balance by removing sucrose solution if the amount of lysate varies by more than 100 μL between samples.
Use a UV detector to monitor and correct the 60S ribosomal fractions, ensuring they do not contaminate 40S or 80S fractions.
Exclude boundary fraction between third and fourth peaks when collecting 60S ribosomal fractions.
Proceed with immunoprecipitation of NEMF-60S RNC.
Purify NEMF-60S RNC by immunoprecipitating V5-TEV-NEMF using anti-V5 antibody from the 60S ribosome fraction.
Digest V5-TEV-NEMF with AcTEV protease to elute immunoprecipitated complexes.
Add 125 μL of anti-V5-Protein G Dynabeads to the 60S fraction in a 15 mL tube per sample.
Rotate tubes at 10 rpm for 1 hour at 4°C.
Place tubes on a magnetic rack, let stand for one minute, and discard supernatant carefully by pipetting.
Transfer beads into a new 1.5 mL tube per sample after washing.
Wash beads with 700 μL of Lysis buffer supplemented with RNasin RNase inhibitor per sample by gentle pipetting.
Repeat wash step three more times.
Wash beads once with 700 μL of Buffer TEV.
Elute the NEMF-60S RNC by digesting V5-TEV-NEMF with 70 units of AcTEV protease in 300 μL of Buffer TEV per sample.
Rotate the tubes at 10 rpm for 2 hours at 4°C.
Place the tube on a magnetic rack and collect the eluate in a new 1.5 mL tube per sample.
Add an equal volume (300 μL) of acidic phenol (pH 4.2) to the eluted complexes above.
Vortex rigorously.
Centrifuge at 15000 g for 10 minutes at 4°C together with the input sample.
Collect approximately 280 μL of the aqueous phase.
Add 300 μL of chloroform to the collected aqueous phase.
Vortex rigorously after adding chloroform.
Centrifuge at 15000 g for 10 min at 4°C.
Collect approximately 250 μL of the aqueous phase from the supernatant.
Add 0.5 μL of 20 mg/mL glycogen to the collected aqueous phase.
Mix well after adding glycogen.
Add 30 μL of 3 M sodium acetate, pH 5.5, and mix well.
Add 750 μL of ethanol and vortex rigorously.
Keep the tubes at –80°C for 1 h.
Centrifuge at 15000 g for 10 min at 4°C.
Carefully aspirate the supernatant.
Add 1 mL of 75% ethanol to the pellet without vortexing.
Centrifuge again at 15000 g for 10 min.
Air dry the pellet.
Resuspend the pellet in 20 μL of ddH2O for the eluted sample and 200 μL for the input sample.
Quantify the RNAs by Nanodrop.
Dilute and denature the input RNA samples by mixing 2 μL of input RNA with ddH2O up to 100 μL.
Heat diluted input RNA samples at 75°C for 10 minutes.
Chill diluted input RNA samples immediately on ice after heating.
Denature eluted RNA samples by mixing 20 μL of eluted RNA with ddH2O up to 100 μL.
Heat denatured eluted RNA samples at 75°C for 10 minutes.
Chill denatured eluted RNA samples immediately on ice after heating.
Mix 2.5 μL of diluted RNA with 2 μL of 10 μM reverse primer for each tRNA in a PCR tube.
Keep the mixture at 65°C for 5 min in a PCR machine.
Chill the mixture on ice immediately after heating.
Add 3 μL of 5× ReverTra Ace RT buffer to the reaction mixture.
Include 3 μL of 10 mM dNTPs in the reaction mixtures.
Add 0.375 μL of RNasin RNase inhibitor to the reaction mixtures.
Mix 0.375 μL of ReverTra Ace Reverse Transcriptase with the reaction mixtures.
Combine 3.75 μL of ddH2O with each sample in the reaction mixtures.
Add 10.5 μL of the reaction mixture to the denatured RNA/primer mixture.
Start the reverse transcription reaction at 55°C for 30 min.
Incubate at 95°C for 5 min after the reverse transcription.
Store the cDNA at 4°C if immediate use is not possible (not recommended).
Prepare the reaction mixtures containing 7.5 μL of 2× KAPA SYBR Fast qPCR mixture.
Add 0.3 μL of 10 μM forward and reverse primers to each sample in the mixtures.
Mix 4.9 μL of ddH2O with each sample for the number of samples needed.
Add 2 μL of cDNA to the reaction mixtures for each tRNA to be tested.
Combine 13 μL of the reaction mixture with the cDNA in a 96 well qPCR plate.
Place the plate in a qPCR machine (BioRad).
Start the preinstalled 2 step protocol with a melt curve step.
